title: Blockchain & Web3 Engineer
description: Architect decentralized applications (dApps), secure smart contracts in Solidity, zero-knowledge proofs, and token economic protocols on Ethereum and EVM chains.

goal.objective: Design, audit, and deploy tamper-proof decentralized applications, smart contract protocols, and Web3 infrastructure across public blockchains.

learn.summary: Master Solidity 0.8+, EVM memory and storage opcodes, Hardhat and Foundry testing suites, OpenZeppelin standards (ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155), and reentrancy defenses.
prerequisites: Solid programming experience (JavaScript, Python, or C++)

capstone_projects.description: Architect a Uniswap v2 style constant-product AMM featuring ERC-20 swap mechanics, liquidity provisioning, reentrancy guards, and Foundry fuzz invariant tests.

capstone_projects.title: Decentralized Collateralized Lending Protocol & Liquidator Bot
capstone_projects.description: Build an overcollateralized lending pool with interest rate curves, Chainlink price feed validation, and an automated off-chain liquidator bot.

interview_focus: Reentrancy Attack Vectors (Single-Function, Cross-Function, Read-Only Reentrancy)
EVM Storage Layout, Slot Packing & Gas Optimization (Calldata vs Memory vs Storage)
ERC-4337 Account Abstraction (UserOperations, Bundlers, Paymasters & Smart Wallets)
Oracle Manipulation Risks, Time-Weighted Average Price (TWAP) & Flash Loan Defenses
Foundry Fuzz Testing, Invariant Handlers & Symbolic Execution Principles

tree.name: Blockchain & Web3 Fundamentals
tree.description: Establish an uncompromising blockchain foundation: master asymmetric cryptography (secp256k1, Keccak-256), distributed consensus mechanisms, cryptographic state trees (Merkle Patricia Tries), and EIP-1559 transaction economics.

resources.title: A beginner's guide to the blockchain

children.name: DLT & Cryptography Basics
children.description: Master applied cryptography for decentralized ledgers: public-key cryptography using elliptic curve secp256k1, cryptographic hashing with Keccak-256 and SHA-256, digital signatures with ECDSA (`r`, `s`, `v` components), recovering signer addresses with `ecrecover`, and zero-knowledge proof primitives.

children.name: Blockchain Architecture & Components
children.description: Understand blockchain node and peer-to-peer network architecture: gossip protocols (libp2p), block anatomy (block header, transactions list, receipts root, state root), consensus models (Proof of Stake Casper FFG, validator slashing conditions, liveness vs safety), and state transition functions.

children.name: Decentralization & Web3 Principles
children.description: Analyze trust minimization and decentralization trade-offs: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT), Sybil attack resistance, the blockchain trilemma (decentralization, security, scalability), and evaluating high-impact decentralized use cases vs centralized architectures.

children.name: Wallets, Keys, and Addresses
children.description: Master Web3 identity and key management: hierarchical deterministic (HD) wallets, mnemonic seeds (BIP-39), master private keys (BIP-32), derivation paths (BIP-44 standard `m/44'/60'/0'/0/x`), deriving Ethereum addresses from public keys via Keccak-256 hashing, hardware wallets, and secure signing workflows.

children.name: Transaction Lifecycle & Gas Model
children.description: Master transaction execution and gas economics: transaction lifecycle (signing, mempool propagation, inclusion, execution, finalization), EIP-155 replay protection, EIP-1559 dynamic fee architecture (base fee burnt by protocol, priority fee / miner tip, max fee per gas), and transaction nonces to prevent double-spending.

tree.name: Ethereum Ecosystem & EVM Deep Dive
tree.description: Master the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) execution environment: state machine transitions, memory and storage slot layouts, opcode gas costs, client diversity, and JSON-RPC specifications.

children.name: Ethereum Account Model & State
children.description: Master Ethereum state architecture: Externally Owned Accounts (EOAs) vs Smart Contract Accounts, account state components (nonce, balance, storageRoot, codeHash), world state representation via Merkle Patricia Tries, and transaction receipt trie logging.

children.name: EVM Architecture & Opcodes
children.description: Deep dive into low-level EVM execution internals: stack-based architecture (1024 stack depth limit, 256-bit word size, `stack too deep` errors), volatile memory (byte-addressable expansion costs), persistent 32-byte storage slots, read-only calldata, and key EVM opcodes (`SSTORE`, `SLOAD`, `DELEGATECALL`, `STATICCALL`, `CREATE2`).

children.name: Ethereum Gas Model & Costs
children.description: Master EVM gas mechanics and optimization: cold vs warm storage access costs (EIP-2929 `SLOAD` 2100 vs 100 gas), storage allocation costs (`SSTORE` 20000 gas for non-zero slot), memory expansion quadratic gas curve, gas refund caps (EIP-3529), and out-of-gas revert mechanics.

children.name: Ethereum Clients & Network Types
children.description: Understand Ethereum infrastructure and client diversity: separation of Execution Clients (Geth, Nethermind, Besu) and Consensus Clients (Prysm, Lighthouse, Teku) via the Engine API, running local validation nodes, and navigating testnets (Sepolia, Holesky) vs Ethereum Mainnet.

children.name: JSON-RPC & Web3 Providers
children.description: Master Ethereum JSON-RPC communication: interacting with nodes via HTTP and WebSocket RPCs (`eth_call`, `eth_sendRawTransaction`, `eth_getLogs`, `eth_estimateGas`), managing rate limits, and utilizing enterprise RPC node infrastructure (Alchemy, Infura, QuickNode).

tree.name: Solidity Programming Language
tree.description: Master Solidity smart contract engineering: language idioms (Solidity 0.8+), storage slot packing, memory pointers, custom errors, and Yul inline assembly optimization.

resources.title: Solidity, Blockchain, and Smart Contract Course (freeCodeCamp)
CryptoZombies - Learn Solidity by Building Games

children.name: Solidity Basics & Data Types
children.description: Master Solidity core types and memory representation: value types (integers with automatic overflow checks in 0.8+, booleans, `address` vs `address payable`), reference types (arrays, strings, structs, mappings), type casting, and understanding storage slot assignment.

children.name: Functions, Modifiers, & Events
children.description: Master contract logic and event emission: function visibility (`external`, `public`, `internal`, `private`), state mutability (`pure`, `view`, `payable`), custom function modifiers and reentrancy execution order, indexed event topics (max 3 indexed topics) for efficient off-chain log filtering.

children.name: Error Handling & Assertions
children.description: Master modern, gas-efficient error handling: replacing expensive `require(cond, 'string')` with custom errors (`revert CustomError()`) to save deployment and runtime gas, `assert()` for checking internal invariant violations, and `try/catch` for handling external contract call failures.

children.name: Storage, Memory, and Calldata
children.description: Master data location semantics and slot packing: `storage` (persistent 32-byte slots; packing multiple smaller types like `uint128` + `uint128` into a single slot to cut gas in half), `memory` (heap-allocated temporary arrays), and `calldata` (immutable read-only zero-copy input parameters saving significant gas).

resources.title: Solidity Storage vs Memory vs Calldata - Solidity Tutorial
Understanding Solidity Data Locations | Storage vs Memory vs Calldata

children.name: Inheritance, Interfaces, & Libraries
children.description: Master contract composition and modularity: multiple inheritance with C3 linearization (resolving the diamond problem), abstract contracts, interfaces for external interoperability, and reusable libraries (internal libraries inlining code vs external libraries deployed with `DELEGATECALL`).

children.name: Contract Deployment & Interaction
children.description: Master contract deployment and funding: initialization in `constructor`, dynamic contract creation with `create` and deterministic address deployment with `create2` (salt-based factory pattern), receiving native Ether via `receive()` and handling unknown calldata via `fallback()`.

children.name: Solidity Advanced Concepts
children.description: Master advanced Solidity and Yul inline assembly: writing inline Yul blocks for ultra-optimized operations (`sload`, `sstore`, `mstore`, custom bit-shifting), user-defined value types (UDVTs), transient storage (`TSTORE`, `TLOAD` via EIP-1153 for cheap reentrancy locks), and signature verification (`ecrecover`).

tree.name: Smart Contract Standards & Design Patterns
tree.description: Implement production-grade smart contract standards and security patterns: ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155, ERC-4626 Tokenized Vaults, role-based access control, and upgradeable proxy architectures.

children.name: ERC Token Standards
children.description: Master Ethereum Improvement Proposals (EIPs) and token standards: ERC-20 fungible tokens (approvals, transferFrom, permit via EIP-2612 signatures), ERC-721 non-fungible tokens, ERC-1155 multi-tokens, and ERC-4626 Tokenized Vault standard for standardized yield-bearing DeFi vaults.

children.name: Common Smart Contract Design Patterns
children.description: Implement essential smart contract architectural patterns: Checks-Effects-Interactions (CEI) to eliminate reentrancy, Pull over Push payment patterns to prevent denial-of-service, Mutex locks, Factory pattern for deterministic contract cloning, and Commit-Reveal schemes to prevent frontrunning.

resources.title: Solidity Design Patterns (OpenZeppelin's Best Practices for Smart Contracts)

children.name: Access Control & Ownership Patterns
children.description: Implement enterprise access control: OpenZeppelin `Ownable2Step` (preventing accidental contract ownership transfer to invalid addresses), and `AccessControlDefaultAdminRules` for granular, role-based access control (RBAC) with administrative delay timers.

children.name: Storage Layout & Upgradeability Fundamentals
children.description: Understand proxy storage collision mechanics: deterministic upgradeable storage layout, unstructured storage pattern (EIP-1967 storage slots), avoiding storage slot collisions when upgrading contracts, and using ERC-7201 namespaced storage layouts.

resources.title: Layout of State Variables in Storage

children.name: Pausable & Advanced Upgradeable Proxy Patterns
children.description: Implement production proxy patterns: Transparent Upgradeable Proxy pattern (separating admin calls from user calls via ProxyAdmin) vs Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard (UUPS with `_authorizeUpgrade` embedded in logic contract for lower deployment and execution gas), and emergency circuit breakers with `Pausable`.

children.name: Secure Contract Design Best Practices
children.description: Design battle-hardened smart contracts: adhering to the OpenZeppelin Contracts library, minimizing external contract calls, validating return values on low-level calls, and implementing fail-safe emergency withdrawal mechanisms.

tree.name: Development Environments & Testing
tree.description: Master the modern smart contract testing and development toolchain: Foundry (Forge, Cast, Anvil), invariant and fuzz testing, and automated CI/CD security pipelines.

children.name: Local Development Tooling
children.description: Master modern high-speed development with Foundry: compiling smart contracts with `forge build`, interacting with chains and inspecting state with `cast`, and running fast local testnet forks with `anvil`.

children.name: Code Quality, Linting & Formatting
children.description: Enforce automated Solidity code standards: automated formatting with `forge fmt`, static linting with `solhint`, and comprehensive NatSpec documentation (`@notice`, `@dev`, `@param`, `@return`) for automated ABI documentation generation.

resources.title: How to Setup Hardhat with Typescript (J-HAYER)

children.name: Debugging Smart Contracts
children.description: Debug complex smart contract execution: transaction tracing with `forge test -vvvv`, setting breakpoints with the Foundry interactive debugger (`forge debug`), inspecting stack and memory states, and analyzing EVM opcode execution step-by-step.

resources.title: Debug and Test Smart Contracts with Hardhat

children.name: Smart Contract Testing Frameworks
children.description: Master comprehensive testing in Foundry: writing unit tests in native Solidity, stateless fuzz testing (`forge test --fuzz-runs`), stateful property-based invariant testing with test handler contracts, cheatcodes (`vm.prank`, `vm.warp`, `vm.roll`, `vm.deal`, `vm.expectRevert`), and forking live Ethereum mainnet state for realistic integration testing.

children.name: Deployment Strategies & Scripting
children.description: Master automated deployment scripting: authoring declarative deployment scripts with `forge script`, managing private keys securely via hardware wallets or encrypted keystores (`cast wallet`), multi-chain deployments, and automated contract verification on Etherscan.

children.name: CI/CD for Smart Contracts
children.description: Build enterprise CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions: running automated formatting checks, executing the full Foundry test suite with invariant tests, generating gas snapshot regression reports (`forge snapshot`), and running automated security scans.

tree.name: Decentralized Application (Dapp) Development
tree.description: Build full-stack Web3 applications: client-side interaction with Viem and Wagmi, multi-wallet connection, event streaming, and decentralized storage.

resources.title: Full Stack Web3 Development with JavaScript (freeCodeCamp)

children.name: Web3 Frontend Libraries
children.description: Master modern, type-safe client libraries: Viem for lightweight, modular, and type-safe EVM interaction (ABI parsing, type inference, contract reading/writing), and Wagmi v2 React hooks for reactive state management.

children.name: Wallet Integration & UX Considerations
children.description: Implement seamless wallet connectivity: multi-wallet onboarding with ConnectKit / RainbowKit / AppKit, supporting EIP-6963 multi-injected provider discovery (MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, Phantom), WalletConnect v2 for mobile wallets, network switching, and graceful error handling for rejected transactions.

children.name: Frontend Frameworks Integration
children.description: Integrate Web3 state in modern Next.js App Router applications: managing server-side rendering (SSR) hydration with Wagmi context providers, handling optimistic UI updates, and tracking transaction confirmation states.

resources.title: Build a Full-Stack Smart Contract Application (Ethereum)

children.name: Interacting with Smart Contracts (Frontend)
children.description: Execute contract transactions and read state from the client: calling `readContract` with automatic polling, simulating transactions with `simulateContract` before prompting user signatures to prevent failed transactions and wasted gas, and waiting for transaction inclusion receipts (`waitForTransactionReceipt`).

resources.title: Read Blockchain Event Logs with eth_getLogs (Alchemy)

children.name: Off-chain Data Processing & Event Handling
children.description: Process on-chain events off-chain: listening to smart contract events via WebSockets, indexing historical event logs with Viem `getLogs`, building backend event indexers in Node.js/Go, and notifying users via webhooks or push notifications.

resources.title: Read Blockchain Event Logs with eth_getLogs (Alchemy)
How to Listen to Ethereum Events with Ethers.js

children.name: IPFS & Decentralized Storage
children.description: Master decentralized immutable storage: InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) content-addressed hashing (CIDv0/CIDv1), pinning NFT metadata and dApp frontend assets using Pinata / Web3.Storage, and integrating with Arweave for permanent decentralized storage.

tree.name: Smart Contract Security & Audits
tree.description: Master smart contract auditing and exploit analysis: identifying attack vectors (reentrancy, flash loans, oracle manipulation), running static analyzers, and participating in bug bounties.

resources.title: Ethernaut - Learn by Hacking Smart Contracts

children.name: Common Vulnerabilities & Exploits
children.description: Master classic and modern smart contract exploit vectors: single-function, cross-function, and read-only reentrancy attacks, flash loan attack mechanics, price oracle manipulation (spot price DEX manipulation vs time-weighted average prices TWAP), frontrunning and Maximal Extractable Value (MEV/sandwich attacks), unprotected initialization, signature replay attacks (missing nonce/chainId in EIP-712), and precision loss / integer division pitfalls.

resources.title: (Not So) Smart Contracts: Solidity Vulnerability Examples
Smart Contract Hacking Course - Learn Solidity & Ethereum Hacking
Solidity, Blockchain, and Smart Contract Course – Beginner to Expert Python Tutorial

children.name: Security Tools & Analysis
children.description: Utilize automated smart contract security tools: running static analysis with Slither to catch common vulnerabilities in CI, symbolic execution with Mythril, mutation testing with Gambit, and introduction to formal verification using Certora Prover or Halmos.

resources.title: Cyber Security Full Course for Beginner
Cyber Security Full Course for Beginner

children.name: Auditing, Bug Bounties & Responsible Disclosure
children.description: Master the security auditing workflow: authoring comprehensive audit reports detailing vulnerability impact and proof-of-concept exploits, participating in competitive audit contests (Code4rena, Sherlock), finding vulnerabilities in live protocols on Immunefi, and responsible disclosure ethics.

resources.title: Cyber Security Full Course for Beginner

tree.name: Advanced Topics & Ecosystem Tools
tree.description: Master advanced Web3 infrastructure: Layer 2 Rollups (Optimistic & ZK), decentralized oracles, GraphQL subgraphs, cross-chain bridges, and ERC-4337 Account Abstraction.

resources.title: Blockchain Layer 2 Scaling Explained | Optimism, Arbitrum, ZK-Rollups, and More

children.name: Layer 2 Scaling Solutions Deep Dive
children.description: Deep dive into Layer 2 scaling architectures: Optimistic Rollups (Arbitrum One, Optimism Bedrock, fault proofs, 7-day challenge periods), Zero-Knowledge Rollups (zkSync Era, Starknet, Polygon zkEVM, validity proofs / SNARKs / STARKs), data availability (EIP-4844 Proto-Danksharding blob transactions, Celestia, EigenDA), and L1-to-L2 message passing.

resources.title: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to Ethereum Scaling
Ethereum Layer 2 Explained - Arbitrum, Optimism, zkSync, StarkWare, and more

children.name: Oracles & Off-Chain Data
children.description: Integrate decentralized oracle networks: Chainlink Data Feeds (price feeds with heartbeat, staleness checks, and deviation thresholds), Chainlink VRF (Verifiable Random Function) for cryptographically provable randomness in gaming/lotteries, Chainlink Automation, and Pyth Network pull oracles.

resources.title: Chainlink Tutorial - Learning Smart Contract Oracles

children.name: Data Indexing & Subgraphs
children.description: Master blockchain data indexing with The Graph: authoring custom Subgraphs (manifest `subgraph.yaml`, GraphQL schema, AssemblyScript event mapping handlers), indexing high-volume contract events, and querying historical blockchain state via GraphQL APIs.

resources.title: The Graph Protocol Course – Build and Deploy a Subgraph

children.name: DAOs & On-Chain Governance
children.description: Architect on-chain and off-chain governance systems: OpenZeppelin `Governor` contracts (proposal submission, voting delay, voting period, quorum, execution timelock), token-weighted voting (ERC20Votes with historical checkpoints), and off-chain gasless voting with Snapshot.

resources.title: What is a DAO? (Decentralized Autonomous Organizations) - Simply Explained
Learn Blockchain, Solidity, and Full Stack Web3 Development with JavaScript – 32-Hour Course

children.name: Cross-Chain Interoperability
children.description: Master cross-chain communication and liquidity: bridge architectures (canonical lock-and-mint vs burn-and-mint), cross-chain messaging protocols (Chainlink CCIP, LayerZero v2, Wormhole), security risks of multi-sig bridges, and building omnichain applications.

resources.title: What is Cross-Chain Interoperability? Blockchain Explained
LayerZero Explained - Omnichain Fungible Tokens (OFTs) in Depth

children.name: Account Abstraction (ERC-4337)
children.description: Master ERC-4337 Account Abstraction: eliminating EOAs with smart contract wallets, understanding `UserOperations`, Bundlers, the canonical `EntryPoint` contract, Paymasters for sponsoring user gas fees (gasless transactions or paying gas in ERC-20 tokens), session keys, and social recovery.

resources.title: ERC-4337: Account Abstraction via Entry Point
What is ERC-4337 Account Abstraction? How Smart Contract Wallets Work
What is Account Abstraction? ERC-4337 (Patrick Collins)
